issues.title: Raise selectivity ratio required to materialize a common multi-table subplan
issues.hypothesis: In q02, CommonSubplanOptimizer turns supplier⋈nation⋈region into a materialized CTE (__common_subplan_1), which both the outer query and the decorrelated min() subquery read. Measured hot, 8 threads, same session, 3 runs each: default 68.1 / 68.5 ms; with SET disabled_optimizers='common_subplan' 47.1 / 51.4 / 52.9 ms, about -25%. Computing the subplan on its own hot costs only about 5 ms, so recomputing it twice costs far less than materializing it does. Materializing costs a full pipeline barrier (CTE child meta-pipeline -> CTE_SCAN build pipeline -> partsupp probe), a copy of all 7 wide string columns, and the loss of the direct table-scan build sides and dynamic join-filter pushdown through the CTE. The rule is IsSelectiveMultiTablePlan (src/optimizer/common_subplan_optimizer.cpp:975). It materializes when est_card <= 2048 or est_card < max_base_card / CARDINALITY_RATIO with ratio 2. Here est_card = 19,230 and max base = 100,000 (ratio 5.2), so only a weakly selective subplan gets materialized. Materializing pays off when the shared subplan is much smaller than the scans it saves. At 2-8x reduction, recomputing in parallel pipelines is cheaper.
issues.plan: In src/optimizer/common_subplan_optimizer.cpp, CommonSubplanFinder::IsSelectiveMultiTablePlan: raise CARDINALITY_RATIO from 2 to 8, so a non-aggregate multi-table subplan above 2048 rows is materialized only when its estimated output is below 1/8 of its largest base table. Leave CARDINALITY_THRESHOLD (2048) and the EndsInAggregateOrDistinct path in ShouldMaterialize unchanged. Verify with EXPLAIN q02.m0 that no __common_subplan CTE remains, that the result matches, and run bench. If the gain is not there, check whether the plan without the CTE differs in join order (EXPLAIN with the optimizer disabled). If it is, the gain comes from that rather than from the barrier, so record which.
issues.expected_gain: q02: about -20 to -25% hot (measured 68 -> 50 ms with the optimizer disabled). The ratio is scale-invariant, and the plan does not depend on the region literal (the estimate is the same for any region).
issues.generality: Helps any query with a repeated join subplan that is only weakly selective (2-8x reduction), for example correlated-subquery decorrelation over a dimension join (TPC-H Q2 shape, other dimension⋈dimension repeats). Strongly selective subplans (e.g. a Q11-style partsupp⋈supplier⋈nation with one nation, ~25x) and aggregate or distinct subplans still get materialized. Could be slower when a weakly selective subplan scans a very large table and recomputing it is expensive.
issues.risk: Low for correctness: it only changes whether an existing, tested rewrite fires, and the result with the rewrite off is the original plan. Moderate performance risk on hidden queries whose 2-8x selective common subplans are expensive to recompute.

dispatch: Raise selectivity ratio required to materialize a common multi-table subplan
output.memory:
# Memory (planner, specialisation run on q02 = TPC-H Q2 shape, SF10)

## Round 1 findings (gen1)
- q02 baseline ~80ms wall. Plan: part scan (p_size=, suffix LIKE) builds HT -> partsupp scan probes with
  a pushed bloom filter (works: 73k of 8M rows survive, "ps_partkey IN BF"); supplier scan probes a
  tiny nation-region HT, result materialised as CTE __common_subplan; the correlated min() subquery is
  decorrelated via LEFT_DELIM_JOIN + HASH_GROUP_BY over the ~6.5k joined rows (cheap).
- Bloom filter pushdown already exists (JoinFilterPushdownInfo in physical_hash_join.cpp). Don't propose "add BF".
- E0001 ACCEPTED (-18.5%): sub-row-group morsels (RowGroupCollection::GetParallelScanMorselVectors).

## Rounds 2-4 (all RETIRED, all "bad idea", not bad implementation)
- E0002 sparse BitPacking select: no gain, so payload decode is not the bottleneck.
- E0003 compaction of sparse scan chunks: no gain, so per-chunk overhead is not the bottleneck.
- E0004 row-level small IN filter on the supplier scan: no gain, because FSST full scans emit lazy vectors.
- Backlog items "Execute tiny dynamic IN filters..." and "Real-row execution of tiny dynamic IN filters" = E0004, DEAD.
- Noise: q02 hot about ±7%; the bar is -5%. Profile operator times are cumulative across threads.

## Round 5 findings (important measurement method)
- Each `dbe-tool sql` call is a fresh process, so the FIRST query is cold (2x slower). Always run the query 2-3 times
  in one sql call (semicolon-separated, $(cat /abs/path/q02.m0.sql) repeated) and read the later "(xx ms)" lines
  with grep -E "ms\)". dbe-tool profile output is from a cold-ish run and is truncated.
- Hot breakdown: supplier⋈nation⋈region alone about 5ms; partsupp⋈part (BF scan) about 17ms; full 5-way join without the
  subquery about 21ms; q02 is about 50-68ms. So the CTE plus the decorrelated subquery machinery adds about 30ms.
- KEY: SET disabled_optimizers='common_subplan' gives q02 68 -> about 50ms (-25%) hot. The CTE comes from
  CommonSubplanFinder::IsSelectiveMultiTablePlan (common_subplan_optimizer.cpp:975): it materializes if est <= 2048
  or est < max_base/2. q02 has est 19,230 vs a 100k base (ratio 5.2).
- DISPATCHED E0005: CARDINALITY_RATIO 2 -> 8. If it fails with no gain, the plan without the CTE may differ in
  another way (join order or filter pushdown); compare EXPLAIN with and without the optimizer. If hidden queries regress,
  try a narrower condition (e.g. skip materializing only when a CTE ref sits under a delim join, or when a
  ref is a hash-join build side that could push filters).
- Partsupp BF scan hot: about 0.06-0.07s cumulative (8M rows, BF on ps_partkey). BloomFilter::LookupHashes is
  simple (bloom_filter.cpp). Possible future lever: the hash cost (VectorOperations::Hash) plus the lookup for 8M rows.
- Pipeline deps: PhysicalCTE::BuildPipelines makes a child meta-pipeline; CTE_SCAN pipelines depend on it
  (physical_column_data_scan.cpp:86). MetaPipeline::AddRecursiveDependencies only adds deps for big sources.

## Codebase facts
- Parallel scan morsel: RowGroupCollection::NextParallelScan (row_group_collection.cpp); now sub-row-group.
- RowGroup::Scan (row_group.cpp:694-824): filters -> col_data.Filter per filter column, then Select for the others.
- StandardColumnData::Select falls back to Scan+Slice without a compression select. FSST and dict_fsst have selects.
- ColumnSegment::FilterSelection (column_segment.cpp:405) has no IN_FILTER case (E0004 added one, but it was retired).
- OptionalFilter::FilterSelection is a no-op; SelectivityOptionalFilter runs its child row-wise with self-disable.
  RowGroup::CheckZonemap treats top-level OPTIONAL_FILTER as always-true.
- JoinFilterPushdownInfo::FinalizeFilters (physical_hash_join.cpp:814): min/max as SelectivityOptional, IN as Optional,
  BF only when the HT is not perfect and the build has a filter.
- supplier storage SF10: 1 row group; s_address Uncompressed 12 segs; partsupp ps_partkey BitPacking 66 segs,
  ps_suppkey/ps_supplycost 131 segs.
- dbe-tool tips: no braces {n}, no awk/sed/head, no `cd ;` compounds, no `~[` in a grep pattern (zsh). Use
  [A-Z_][A-Z_][A-Z_]+ instead of {n}. `| tr '\n' ' '` after grep -o needs approval; plain grep works.

## Directions
- Promising: optimizer-level plan choices (CTE materialization). Measure them with disabled_optimizers first; that
  is a cheap way to test whole optimizer passes before filing an issue.
- Exhausted: scan-level decode/filter micro-optimizations on q02 (E0002-E0004).
